summary: Inference-lane crosstalk: KV-prefetch amplification causing GPU attach starvation in dedicated pool
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports sustained p99 latency and sudden drop in throughput for several batched routes served from their dedicated pool. Impact: LumenAI experienced ~40% drop in steady-state throughput and higher tail latency across short inference streams, causing timeouts for user-facing features.
Environment: Dedicated pool (tenant id: lumen-1976) in us-east-1 serving chat and generate endpoints. Autoscale configured with burst capacity and prefetch enabled for long-context routes.
Observed behavior: Gradual queueing, followed by repeated GPU attach failures and autoscaler refusing additional allocations for ~6 minute windows. Metrics show an unexpected spike in kv-cache prefetch requests and a correlated increase in short-stream attach attempts.
Expected behavior: Prefetch should reduce token work and not cause cross-tenant amplification or attach starvation. Autoscaler should react with graceful scaling rather than stall.
Steps to reproduce: (1) Customer ran steady low-QPS short chat traffic plus intermittent long-context transcripts. (2) Enabled server-side KV prefetch on the long-context model variant. (3) At ~11:18 local time the pool throughput fell and requests began observing 503/attach-timeout.
Immediate mitigation desired: Identify safe rollback for prefetch behavior or temporary autoscaler policy tweak to avoid starvation while preserving isolation.
steps_to_reproduce: Mix low-latency short streams with intermittent long-context prefetch-enabled requests against a dedicated pool.
Enable aggressive kv-cache prefetch (thresholds tuned to aggressively prefetch full prefixes).
Observe sustained attach queue growth and repeated attach timeouts in pool-level metrics.
logs: metrics snapshot: kv_prefetch_rate=860 req/s (baseline 40 req/s), alloc_failures=12, autoscaler_shrink_events=3
comments: 2026-03-10 11:30 - Aisha Patel (Support): Acknowledged the report and escalated to SRE. Asked customer to capture a short tracer and turned on request-level debug logs.

2026-03-10 12:05 - Marco Ruiz (SRE): Confirmed correlated spike in kv-prefetch rate from tenant. Dashboard: /dashboards/dedicated/pool/lumen-1976. Hypothesis: prefetch amplification on long-context routes is generating many ephemeral allocations that crowd out short-stream attach slots.
2026-03-10 12:20 - LumenAI (Customer): Provided heap of logs and said the prefetch tuning was recently increased to reduce long-context cold-starts.

2026-03-10 13:02 - Marco Ruiz (SRE): Applied temporary autoscaler policy change for lumen-1976 to raise attach reservation for short-stream routes (policy id: short-stream-protect-2026-03-10). Monitoring impact.
2026-03-10 13:25 - Aisha Patel (Support): Updated customer: temporary mitigation applied; asked to hold prefetch tuning at previous level while we investigate.
2026-03-11 09:10 - Eng Lead (Nora Chen): Noted similar telemetry patterns to SUP-314159; suggested implementing prefetch backpressure to limit concurrent prefetches per tenant.

2026-03-12 10:40 - Marco Ruiz (SRE): Reproduced amplification in staging with synthetic traffic; confirmed race between prefetch requests creating short-lived allocation spikes and the allocator's fairness heuristics.

2026-03-12 15:00 - Marco Ruiz (SRE): Proposed longer-term fixes and scheduled rollout of a mitigation patch to the serving-runtime that adds prefetch concurrency limits and a per-tenant prefetch token bucket.
investigation_notes: 11:32 - Pull from monitoring: prefetched_kv_hits rose 20x at onset; prefetch concurrency per-request rose from 1 to 8 due to new tuning on customer side.
12:12 - Scheduler logs show many short-lived allocations with lifetime < 25s, leading to allocator slot thrashing and elevated attach latencies.

12:40 - Autoscaler telemetry: scale-up proposals were suppressed due to a safety gate that interprets transient small allocations as noise (see PR 4821 discussion). Safety gate prevented scaling during sustained but noisy attach churn.
13:05 - Reproduction in staging: synthetic long-context requests with aggressive prefetch replicate queue depth and attach failures; limiting prefetch concurrency restores steady throughput.

13:50 - Root cause hypothesis: KV-prefetch amplification (customer tuning) created many concurrent ephemeral allocation attempts that exhausted attach bandwidth and triggered autoscaler safety heuristics, producing temporary GPU shortage for other routes.
14:30 - Risk assessment: high customer impact during peak windows; potential to affect other tenants in same reserved pool if prefetch behavior unchecked.

2026-03-11 - Correlation to previous incidents: patterns are distinct from classic noisy-neighbor CPU-heavy workloads; this is an I/O/attach pattern amplified by prefetch logic and autoscaler safety gating.
resolution_notes: Mitigation applied (2026-03-10 13:02): temporary autoscaler policy tweak to reserve attach capacity for short-stream routes; immediate reduction in p99 latency observed.

Workaround recommended to customer: revert prefetch concurrency to previous safe defaults and avoid aggressive prefetch tuning until runtime patch deploys. Customer agreed and rolled back changes on 2026-03-10 14:00.

Short-term fix (planned rollout 2026-03-15): implement per-tenant prefetch concurrency limiter + token-bucket to prevent amplification spikes. Patch PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4887.
Medium-term fix: update autoscaler safety gate to recognize sustained attach churn patterns and prefer slot reservation over shrink decisions for prefetch-heavy workloads.

Follow-ups: add a dedicated alert for sudden kv-prefetch amplification and a one-click console control for tenants to throttle prefetch; notify product to consider prefetch tuning presets for dedicated customers.
Post-incident actions: schedule a postmortem with LumenAI and internal engineering; add a runbook entry to confluence page referenced above.
